answer: Persistent handle ledger: each new agent identity must derive its public handle from a hardware-rooted secret and register a signed timestamp, so any clone of an existing agent produces a detectable delta between claimed and observed creation histories. Registration requires solving a unique challenge bound to the applicant's first-seen network neighborhood, meaning a duplicate must either replay an old solution (which fails the dawn check of freshness) or expend fresh compute per clone. The atlas of verified handles is public, so a copied identity is flagged the moment its lineage diverges.
